evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 / Chinese Character Database, CUHK
evidence.field: 字形、說文、形義通解、用例
evidence.text: The entry records 快 under its heart/mind radical, lists a small-seal form and four Chu manuscript examples, and gives the Shuowen account 喜也。从心，夬聲 (‘joyful; from 心, with 夬 as phonetic’). Its interpretation connects the early sense ‘joyful’ with later ‘pleased/at ease’; it cites 易·旅 得其資斧，心未快也, Song Yu’s 戰國風賦 快哉此風, 荀子·大略 on 快 as uninhibited/self-indulgent (via Yang Liang’s gloss), and 史記·項羽本紀 快戰 ‘fight vigorously/decisively’. The entry says 快 later commonly means ‘rapid’; it also gives a Tang Du Fu example for ‘sharp’ and a modern literary example for adverbial ‘soon’. These citations document uses, but the source does not date each textual witness independently.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 快

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 / Chinese Character Database, CUHK
evidence.text: The entry for 夬 lists bronze, oracle-bone and manuscript image examples, with 23 of 27 manuscript examples displayed, and gives a separate Shuowen headword 叏: ‘分決也。从又、…象決形’ (‘divide/decide; from 又 and a graph interpreted as depicting cutting through’). It records the Guangyun fanqie 古賣 and Middle Chinese classification 見母, 去聲, 夬韻, 合口二等. This differs from assuming that 快’s phonetic component has a single, securely established original pictorial referent: the page preserves 夬/叏 graphic and lexical accounts but does not establish a direct ancestry for 快’s sound component.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 夬

evidence.field: 快《說文解字注》及歷史釋義
evidence.text: The page reproduces the Shuowen gloss 喜也 and analysis 从心夬聲, then quotes the Shuowen commentator’s statement that 疾速 (‘rapid’) is an extended sense and that the俗字 is 駃. It also lists 快’s senses including satisfying/agreeable, brisk/rapid, indulgent, illness (‘unwell’), and surname. This supports separating documented extensions from original graphic formation; the page does not establish the steps or dates linking all listed senses.
evidence.title: 快 kuài - 汉典

evidence.text: The page records 夬 guài as ‘divide/decide’ and the name of the 43rd hexagram, and a distinct jué reading for a thumb-ring/tool used to open a bowstring, damage, and ‘vacancy’ (通缺), with Qin-slip citations for damage and vacancy. Its Shuowen text is under 叏, ‘分決也。从又…象決形’. This is evidence for multiple lexical uses/readings and graph accounts, not proof that the thumb-ring name was the original sound borrowed by 快.
evidence.title: 夬 guài、jué - 汉典

evidence.field: Old Chinese phonetic-series comparison and readings
evidence.text: The entry groups 快 with 夬 in Zhengzhang Shangfang’s phonetic series and gives Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese 快 *kʰʷraːds and 夬 *kʷraːds; the reconstructed forms differ in initial aspiration but share the rhyme sequence. The same page displays Baxter–Sagart 夬 /*[k]ʷˤret-s/. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV must take precedence for the pair: it has 夬 /*[k]ʷˤret-s/ and 快 /*[k]ʷʰˤret-s/, with explicit uncertain-initial notation for 夬 and distinct aspiration for 快. The rendered secondary source does not provide the corresponding 快 Baxter–Sagart value on the inspected lines, so the local comparison is reported as local evidence rather than attributed to that page.
evidence.title: 快 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: 夬 glyph origin and historical forms
evidence.text: The entry’s glyph-origin section labels 夬 a pictogram, with an asserted interpretation as a hand wearing an archer’s thumb ring, citing Li Xueqing (2012); it also presents historical-form categories for Shang, Western Zhou, Warring States and the Han Shuowen period, but attributes most images to Richard Sears’ Chinese Etymology site and collections including Jinwen Bian and Yinxu Jiaguwen Bian. Because the page’s image display was not visually inspected here and its pictorial interpretation is not established by the opened primary dictionary account alone, this is a reported proposal, not a settled referent. It does not demonstrate that the object’s name was pronounced like 快 or that 快 borrowed a whole graph for that object-name.
evidence.title: 夬 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: 快《說文解字注》及楚簡字形目錄
evidence.text: The page reproduces the explanation that rapidity is an extension of 快 and lists Chu-script manuscript examples, a Shuowen small-seal example and clerical-script examples including Western Han and Eastern Han specimens. This gives a broad graphic sequence from Chu manuscripts through seal and clerical forms, but the page does not describe specific stroke-by-stroke changes or identify any corruption; no glyph image was visually inspected for this research.
evidence.title: 快 kuài - 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 / Chinese Character Database, CUHK
evidence.field: source-text citations under 形義通解
evidence.text: The entry cites 易·旅 得其資斧，心未快也 as an early textual occurrence with the ‘satisfied/pleased’ sense; cites Song Yu’s 風賦 快哉此風 for an exclamation of pleasure; and quotes 史記·項羽本紀 願為諸君快戰 for a vigorous/decisive action sense. It presents these as examples along a semantic account; the page does not provide manuscript dates for the quoted passages, so these cannot by themselves establish precise first-attestation dates or a complete chronological order.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 快

evidence.source: Local Baxter–Sagart transcription cross-check; upstream dictionary page inspected for the phonological comparison
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows 1121 and 1913; externally inspected corroborating page lines 289–323
evidence.text: Local rows: 夬 U+592C has Modern guài, Middle Chinese kwaejH, Old Chinese *[k]ʷˤret-s, gloss ‘divide, make a breach’; 快 U+5FEB has Modern kuài, Middle Chinese khwaejH, Old Chinese *[k]ʷʰˤret-s, gloss ‘cheerful’. The checked TSV notation distinguishes the two Old Chinese initials; it must not be silently merged with Zhengzhang’s separate system (*kʷraːds vs *kʰʷraːds). The opened Wiktionary page displays the Baxter–Sagart value for 夬 and the Zhengzhang series comparison, but its inspected section does not display the 快 Baxter–Sagart row.
evidence.title: 夬 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The page lists 快’s modern Mandarin as kuài and Cantonese as faai3, Japanese on-reading KAI and kun-reading KOKOROYOI, Korean KHWAY and Vietnamese khoái. Its Middle Chinese category is 溪母, 夬韻, 去聲, 快小韻, 苦夬切, 二等合口. These are dictionary readings; the page’s Tang reading and cross-language forms do not independently date the character’s formation.
evidence.title: 快 kuài - 汉典

evidence.field: 字形、說文、形義通解、用例
evidence.text: The entry shows one small-seal example and four Chu manuscript examples for 快, but no oracle-bone or bronze forms. It gives the Shuowen analysis 喜也。从心，夬聲, and presents ‘joyful/pleased’ as the original sense. It cites 易·旅 心未快也 for ‘pleased/satisfied’, Song Yu’s 風賦 快哉此風 for pleasure, 荀子·大略 for an uninhibited sense, 史記·項羽本紀 快戰 for vigorous action, a Tang Du Fu line for ‘sharp’, and a modern literary example for adverbial ‘soon’. These are textual citations, not independently dated manuscript witnesses or a complete semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 快

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry treats 𢘦 as a variant of 快 and says it derives directly from the seal form through clerical transformation; it reports that the Zhengzitong says 𢘦 was the original form and 快 a popular abbreviation, with later omission of 叏 in favor of 夬. This is an explicit historical analysis from the dictionary, but the precise chronology and documentary basis are not established by this page alone.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》: 𢘦 (快)

gaps: No securely dated first attestation of 快 was established; CUHK lists Chu manuscript forms and early textual citations but does not date the individual manuscripts or establish the relative dates of all senses.

The earliest depicted referent and original pronunciation of 夬 remain uncertain across the consulted accounts: Shuowen explains 叏 as ‘divide/decide’, while a secondary proposal identifies 夬 as a thumb ring. No evidence found that 快 is a whole-graph phonetic loan from an object-name; available accounts support 夬 as the sound element within the 心/忄 compound.

The semantic path from the original ‘joyful/pleased’ sense to ‘rapid’, ‘sharp’, ‘indulgent’, ‘unwell’, and adverbial ‘soon’ is not fully established. Shuowen commentary explicitly treats ‘rapid’ as extended; other senses are documented but their chronology and connecting steps remain underdetermined.

No claim of graphic corruption is supported by inspected text. CUHK records distinct 叏 and 夬 headforms/entries; Han Dian says 快 was originally written 𢘦 and popularly abbreviated to 快, but the basis and exact direction/date of that statement were not independently verified here.

Official per-character Unihan pages for U+5FEB and U+592C could not be inspected in the browser. Local Unihan rows were checked, but the required official character-specific click-through verification failed.
Local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked exactly: 快 *[k]ʷʰˤret-s vs 夬 *[k]ʷˤret-s. This differs in notation from Zhengzhang (2003) *kʰʷraːds vs *kʷraːds; the systems are not merged.

No securely dated first attestation of 快 was established. The CUHK page lists Chu manuscript forms and literary citations, but does not independently date the manuscript witnesses or establish a complete chronological order among senses.

The semantic link from ‘joyful/pleased’ to ‘rapid’ is described by the Shuowen commentary as extension in the dossier; the finer steps and dates are unestablished. Other listed meanings, including sharp, indulgent, and soon, are cited but not fully ordered.

The earliest depicted referent and original pronunciation of 夬 are uncertain. The available evidence supports 夬 as a sound component within 快, not a whole-graph loan based on the name of a depicted object. The object's name is not independently recovered here.
MOE’s account says 𢘦 is an original form and 快 a later abbreviated form, but exact chronology and underlying witnesses need corroboration. No graphic corruption claim is established.

Exact official Unicode GetUnihanData records for 快 and 夬 could not be opened, and no accessible exact rows were verified in this stage; modern readings above are reported from local cross-check metadata only.

No image candidate is returned: searches did not establish an accessible direct glyph image with exact identity and provenance. Xiaoxuetang's CC0 terms were verified, but no 快 query result was located. CUHK page glyphs were not visually inspected and its page does not itself provide reuse permission for image assets.
